title: Leek and Potato Soup
subtitle: Silky blended soup of leek and floury potato
excerpt: Leeks and potatoes simmered in vegetable stock until completely tender, then blended smooth with a splash of cream. Simple, clean, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Leek and potato soup is a British classic, closely related to the French vichyssoise (which adds cream and is served cold). The British version is almost always served hot. The combination of leek and potato is ancient in British cooking: both grew well in the British Isles and appeared together in pottages from medieval times. The modern blended version is a 20th century development, enabled by the domestic blender. The soup needs very little seasoning beyond salt: the leeks provide sweetness and depth, and the potatoes give body.

recipeTools.notes: And a stick blender or jug blender.

content.text: Use floury potatoes: they break down more easily and give a smoother result when blended. Simmer until the potatoes are completely soft before blending, or the soup will be grainy. If using a jug blender, blend in batches and allow steam to escape: a tightly sealed lid on a hot liquid can cause the top to blow off.

items.preparation: white and pale green parts, sliced

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and leeks. Cook gently for 10 minutes until softened but not coloured. Add the garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender.
Blend until completely smooth. Stir in the cream. Season with salt and pepper. Reheat gently without boiling. Serve with crusty bread.
